newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp sees no U.S. unit sale plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp sees no U.S. unit sale plan.

text.p: Appliance, packaging and wine group Southcorp Holdings Ltd's managing director Graham Kraehe said on Wednesday it had no plans to sell its loss-making American Water Heater group, formerly Mor-Flo.
The American Water Heater group has lost money for Southcorp ever since it bought the business in July 1992. The division recorded a loss of US$2.5 million in the year to June 30, 1996.

"Today we have plenty of options for that business, to continue the growth programme or, if we wanted to, we could divest it, whereas two years ago that wasn't an option," Kraehe told reporters after a Securities Institute of Australia lunch.
"The American Water Heater group, is not a huge issue for Southcorp today. It certainly was two years ago," Kraehe said.
Earlier, Kraehe told the luncheon that Southcorp planned to make some business divestments.
"The assessment of a divestment is whether it is a business that we can create shareholder value," Kraehe.
Asked whether Southcorp could make a profit or create shareholder value from the American Water Heater group, Kraehe replied: "Yes."
Kraehe said divestment would be more in the packaging business.
"The broad thrust is to direct the packaging business, which is very diverse, from everything that was conceivably packaging to the best part of the portfolio which has strong growth," Kraehe said.
